explanation: The Jacobian matrix is \(\begin{pmatrix}2u&0&-2w\\we^u&0&e^u\\1&-1&0\end{pmatrix}\). Expanding along the second column gives \(2e^u(u+w^2)\). Since \(e^u>0\), the determinant vanishes exactly when \(u=-w^2\), with v arbitrary.

answers.correct_value: The critical points lie on the parabolic cylinder $u=-{w}^{2}.$
